purpose: Final actual-native CPAL xrun verification, after fixes, separate from simulated ratings

variation.name: One explicit visible Play retry after startup output failure
variation.audio_directory: a (short name keeps native UNIX socket path within107 bytes; no backend setting changes)
variation.policy: Keep initial failure and old/new engine IDs; never clear a failed latch or automatically retry. The optional retry is one explicit visible Play command.

startup: Healthy initial playback; conditional explicit Play retry was not needed and was not sent.

post_reference_pcm.method: Capture frame offsets observed at two snapshots at least one second after resume; avoids attributing pre-stall queued samples to recovery.

conclusion: After a 250 ms scheduler stall, the real output-backend dropout counter increased from 0 to 1 and the same engine continued consuming frames with output_failed=false, zero render errors, and 4.116 seconds of nonzero finite post-resume PCM. This supports actual CPAL xrun continuation for the final build in this virtual ALSA/Pulse laboratory. The frozen before build had latched an actual xrun as fatal and emitted silent post-resume PCM.
limits: The final run did not exercise explicit Play retry after a failed engine; that path needs its separate automated test evidence.
Three earlier revised-build attempts hit startup ALSA EIO before consuming any frames; they remain preserved and are not reclassified or claimed fixed by this result.
The application accepts backend recovery of a recoverable xrun; this is not recovery of a terminal EIO stream.
No hardware latency, audible quality, general VST compatibility or revised participant-rating claim follows from this controlled technical replay.
